title: 心理研究词汇
goal: 辨认心理研究词汇，读懂实验设计与研究发现。

points.label: 辨认心理研究的常用词
读懂实验设计与研究发现

body.p: 心理研究常比较人在记忆任务或注意任务中的表现。阅读时分清四样东西：参与者、任务、研究者改变的条件、记录的结果。

body.box: Participants studied a list in silence or with background sound. The researchers recorded how many words each person recalled.

body.p: participants 是参与者；学习词表是任务；声音条件是比较的变量；回忆出的词数是记录的结果。

body.box: A researcher asked two groups to study the same pictures. One group worked in silence; the other heard a quiet tone. Both groups then selected previously seen pictures from a mixed set. The researcher recorded the number of correct selections in each group.

body.p: 参与者的任务是学习并识别图片。两组的不同条件是有无声音，记录的结果是正确选择的数量。
previously seen pictures 是要认出的目标。这段只说明了测量方式，没有说哪一组表现更好。

groups.fill: Researchers can study how people remember words. Each parti{cipant} reads a short list and completes a ta{sk} after a short de{lay}. The researcher records the number of words they rec{all}. A retrieval c{ue}, such as a category name, can be supplied before the test. Another gr{oup} completes the same test without this prompt. The two conditions can then be comp{ared}. The res{ult} describes performance in this particular sam{ple}; another experiment can test whether the fin{ding} is repeated.
notes: finding：另一实验可验证该发现。

groups.text: A researcher asked volunteers to watch a screen and press a key when a circle changed colour. In one condition a tone sounded during the task; in another the room was silent. The researcher measured response time and counted missed changes. The sound condition produced more missed changes in this small sample, while average response times were similar.

options: To press a key after a colour change
To produce a tone after a key press
To choose a quieter room for the test
To count the missed colour changes
items.why: 依据是 press a key when a circle changed colour，第一项是它的改写。数漏掉的变化是研究者的事，第四项把做事的人换了。

items.stem: Which condition was compared with silence?
items.why: 依据是 In one condition a tone sounded during the task; in another the room was silent。与安静条件对照的是有声音的条件，即第二项。

options: The time before the colour changed
The time taken to press the key
items.why: response time 是从颜色变化到按键所用的时间，即第三项。漏掉的变化是另一项计数，第一项把两项测量混在了一起。

items.stem: What was reported about missed changes?
options: They were about equal in both conditions
They were absent in the sound condition
They were more frequent with sound
items.why: 依据是 The sound condition produced more missed changes，即第四项。原文说 similar 的是平均反应时间，第一项把它换到了漏看次数上。

options: The tones played during the task
The colour changes on the screen
The keys pressed during each task
items.why: 依据是 in this small sample。sample 指参加本次研究的志愿者，即第一项。

groups.fill: A study can compare performance under different conditions. Each parti{cipant} completes the same ta{sk}, and the researcher records each resp{onse}. One gr{oup} works with background sound, while the other works in silence. The researchers mea{sure} how long each response takes and count errors on every tr{ial}. They then com{pare} the two conditions. The res{ult} applies directly to this particular sam{ple}. Repeating the experiment can show whether the fin{ding} occurs again in another group.

groups.text:
Three researchers examined how brief interruptions relate to performance on a visual task. The volunteers in their project watched a sequence of shapes and pressed a key whenever a triangle appeared. All participants saw the same sequence, and the researchers recorded both missed triangles and response times. The work was designed to compare conditions within this task rather than to measure every form of attention.

Leah Brooks designed the first comparison. In one condition the sequence continued without interruption. In the other, a short message appeared on the screen halfway through. Participants read the message before returning to the shapes. Brooks found that more triangles were missed immediately after the message than during the equivalent part of the uninterrupted sequence. This finding concerned missed targets; it was not a measure of how well the message itself was remembered.

Daniel Cole analysed the time taken to press the key. In his analysis, responses immediately after the message were slower on average than responses at the equivalent point without a message. He did not count missed triangles as slow responses, because a missed triangle produced no key press to time. Cole also examined variation between participants and reported that the average did not describe every individual equally.

Finally, Amina Field investigated whether the message's content mattered. She compared a message about the task with a message about an unrelated topic. Both appeared at the same point in the sequence. In this sample, the two messages were followed by similar numbers of missed triangles. Field proposed repeating the comparison with other messages. The team's report kept her proposed follow-up separate from the completed comparisons.

items.stem: Who designed the comparison with and without a message? Options may be used more than once.
items.why: 依据是 Leah Brooks designed the first comparison，比较的是有无信息两种条件，即第一项。

items.stem: Who analysed the time taken to press the key? Options may be used more than once.
items.why: 依据是 Daniel Cole analysed the time taken to press the key，即第二项。Brooks 统计的是漏掉的三角形，不是反应时间。

items.stem: Who compared two kinds of message content? Options may be used more than once.
items.why: 依据是 She compared a message about the task with a message about an unrelated topic，She 指 Amina Field，即第三项。

items.stem: Who examined how brief interruptions relate to performance on a visual task? Options may be used more than once.
items.why: 依据是首句 Three researchers examined how brief interruptions relate to performance on a visual task。这是三人共同的研究问题，即第四项。

items.stem: Who reported that average response time did not describe every individual equally? Options may be used more than once.
items.why: 依据是 Cole also examined variation between participants and reported that the average did not describe every individual equally，即第二项。
